newsitem.title: UK: Amoco sees flat chemical earnings in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Amoco sees flat chemical earnings in 1997/98.

text.p: Amoco Corp expects earnings form its chemicals business to be relatively flat worldwide both this year and in 1998, executive vice-president Enrique Sosa said on Thursday.
He told Reuters Financial Television that chemical earnings would, however, see an upturn thereafter.
Although earnings were "strong" in the first half of this year, additional capacity is expected to impact on the second half leaving earnings flat for the year as a whole.

The division on Monday reported an annual drop in first quarter earnings to $147 million, although Sosa pointed out this was an improvement on the previous quarter's $105 million. Chemicals had net income of $735 million in 1996.
Sosa was visiting London to promote the company's European expansion plans.
Amoco is the world's second largest producer of polypropylene with a production capacity of around 1.2 million tons.
On Wednesday, Amoco announced plans to boost its global polypropylene manufacturing capacity by 330,000 tons.
Polypropylene is used in a variety of plastics and fibres including appliances, packaging, automotive components and carpet yarns and backing.
Amoco is the world's biggest producer of PTA.
